<Section title="Final answer">
<RichText>
**Short version: don't.** All three models independently agree that SQLite over NFS or SMB with multiple machines is unsafe: POSIX advisory locking is broken or unreliable on most network-filesystem implementations, so two writers can corrupt the database. WAL mode is ruled out entirely — it coordinates through shared memory (the `-shm` file, via mmap), which cannot work across machines.

What to do instead, in order of preference:

- **Replicate instead of sharing the file.** Run SQLite locally and replicate with Litestream or LiteFS, or step up to a client-server database if you truly need concurrent writers. *(google · gemini-3)*
- **Single client only:** if exactly one machine ever touches the file, `PRAGMA locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE` plus rollback-journal mode is workable. *(openai · gpt-5.2)*
- **Last resort:** the `unix-dotfile` VFS replaces POSIX locks with lock files, dodging broken NFS locking at a real performance and robustness cost. *(anthropic · fable-5)*

**One claim stayed unresolved:** gpt-5.2 says NFSv4 with a correctly configured lock daemon is acceptable for low-concurrency use; fable-5 says no network filesystem is ever safe. Both positions are shown; verify against SQLite's own documentation before relying on either (see "To verify").

*Tags name the contributing vendor and model. Full raw answers are linked under the chain below.*
</RichText>
</Section>

<Section title="Knowledge map">
<Tabs>
<Tab label="Shared core (3/3)">
<RichText>
Claims all three extractors made independently — repetition, not proof:

- POSIX advisory locking (`fcntl`) is unreliable on many NFS/SMB implementations → concurrent writers can corrupt the file.
- WAL mode needs the shared-memory `-shm` file (mmap) → impossible across machines, full stop.
- The common symptom of trying anyway is spurious `database is locked` errors, then silent corruption later.
</RichText>
</Tab>
<Tab label="Unique finds">
<RichText>
Kept even with a support count of one — consensus is repetition, not truth:

- **gpt-5.2 only:** `PRAGMA locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE` makes single-client use on a network mount workable.
- **gemini-3 only:** Litestream / LiteFS replication sidesteps the problem entirely; usually the right architecture.
- **fable-5 only:** the `unix-dotfile` VFS swaps POSIX locks for lock files; slow but immune to broken NFS locking.
- **gemini-3 only (via review round):** SMB behaves differently from NFS — oplocks/lease breaks add their own failure mode; the two should not be lumped together.
</RichText>
</Tab>
<Tab label="Contradictions (1)">
<Callout tone="risk">
**gpt-5.2 vs fable-5, unresolved.** gpt-5.2: NFSv4 with a correctly configured lock daemon is acceptable for low-concurrency workloads. fable-5: no network filesystem is ever safe for shared SQLite. The curator did not pick a side — both positions appear in the final answer, flagged, with a verification target.
</Callout>
</Tab>
